class: T4 hardware-bound diagnostic (no route selection, no target change)
originating_constraint: P40000 decode step 207.4 ms (unroll-8) vs 10 tok/s target (100 ms/step); user question '265K 以内理论速度,找问题'

hardware.measured_pure_read_method: 4 GB float4 read-accumulate kernel, grid 512x256, /tmp/q3x_readbw.cu (removed after use)
hardware.d2d_note: D2D memcpy is read+write bidirectional; NOT a valid pure-read denominator (earlier attribution JSON used 95.4 and understated efficiency by ~2x; corrected in qwen36-27b-p40000-decode-step-attribution-2026-09-26.json CORRECTION section)

theoretical_curve_batch_one.model: step_ms = W/BW + KV_read_floor + compute_residual; W=18.52 GB, pure-read BW=182.5 GB/s
theoretical_curve_batch_one.p40000_absolute_ceiling: CORRECTED 2026-09-26: the earlier '~116 ms/step (~8.6 tok/s)' assumed the values/scores floors were DRAM-bound (7.5 + 7.2 ms). In fact both are L2-bound and already at their practical ceiling (values 40.3 ms, scores 38.6 ms at S=40000, unroll-128). The realistic batch-one ceiling is weight floor 101.5 + values 40.3 + scores 38.6 + launch ~0.7 = ~181 ms/step (~5.5 tok/s); the measured 193.0 ms/step (5.18 tok/s) is within ~6% of it. The 10 tok/s target (100 ms/step) remains below the 101.5 ms weight-read floor and is unreachable for batch-one on this device.

target_reachability.claim: 10 tok/s (100 ms/step) is below the batch-one weight-read hardware floor of 101.5 ms (9.85 tok/s) for this model on this device
target_reachability.evidence: same-workload hardware bound: W=18.52 GB exact per-step read / 182.5 GB/s measured pure-read ceiling; matched profile: GEMV path runs at ~100% of the measured pure-read ceiling (floor 101.5 ms vs measured 103.17 ms intercept from 3-point fit); reconciliation: no known implementation can read 18.52 GB per step in <100 ms on this device
target_reachability.attention_kv_read_efficiency: CORRECTED 2026-09-26: the earlier '9.5% of pure-read ceiling' figure divided the 6x GQA-redundant requested volume (491.5 MB/layer) by the DRAM pure-read ceiling and is misleading. The values kernel at unroll-128 sustains 195 GB/s and the scores kernel 204 GB/s of requested volume -- both ABOVE the 182.5 GB/s DRAM pure-read ceiling, which is only possible because L2 absorbs the 6x GQA redundant reads at near-zero DRAM cost (DRAM carries ~1x unique volume). The attention KV read is therefore L2-bound, not DRAM-bound, and is already at its practical ceiling.

rejected_direction.name: 6-chain GQA-redundancy-free values merge (6144 -> 1024 threads, 6 position-chains per thread)
rejected_direction.verdict: rejected: 3.7x slower; occupancy collapse (1024 threads) dominates; ILP cannot recover; initial illegal-memory-access was a benchmark bug (probability index must advance +1 per position, not +S)

accepted_direction.name: deep unroll of the position-ordered FMA chain (bit-exact: FMA order unchanged)

production_result.bit_exact_test: q3x_decode_ops_cuda_test ATTENTION_VALUE_BINARY_IDENTITY status=PASS; resources unchanged (regs=40, static_shared=0, local=0, active_blocks=6)
production_result.p40000_api: decode_after_first 2895.22 ms / 15 steps = 193.01 ms/step = 5.18 tok/s (unroll-8: 207.39 ms/step = 4.82 tok/s); 16 completion tokens byte-identical to unroll-8 baseline; body sha256 6fb5c1ce...; evidence .q3x-work/evidence/decode-unroll128-api-20260926/

owner_decision_request: 10 tok/s target exceeds the batch-one hardware floor. Options requiring owner ruling: (a) change contract to batched decode (multiple concurrent requests amortize the 18.52 GB weight read); (b) lower weight quantization (accuracy risk, out of current production accuracy scope); (c) re-set the P40000 target to a reachable value (e.g. 8 tok/s absolute ceiling is ~8.6, realistic ~5.2 after unroll-128). This record does not select a route or change the target.

l2_absorption_and_smem_merge.finding: The 6x GQA redundant K/V reads in the exact S>=65 attention kernels are absorbed by L2 at near-zero DRAM cost. Evidence: the values kernel (unroll-128) sustains 195 GB/s and the scores kernel 204 GB/s of requested (6x-redundant) volume per layer, both exceeding the 182.5 GB/s DRAM pure-read ceiling; only L2 hits on the 5 redundant copies explain this. The GEMV weight path runs at 179.5 GB/s (98.4% of the DRAM ceiling), the true DRAM-bound component.

smem_gqa_merge.name: shared-memory GQA merge: one block per KV head serves all 6 query heads from a single smem V tile, reducing the V read from 6x to 1x
smem_gqa_merge.bit_exact: PASS (S=1024 vs CPU oracle, 0/6144 diff) -- the per-(query,dimension) position-ordered FMA sequence is preserved, so the BF16 output is bit-identical
smem_gqa_merge.occupancy: prod 24 blocks x 256 thr (6 blocks/SM); smem 4 blocks x 1024 thr (1 block/SM, sm_87 max 1024 thr/block)
smem_gqa_merge.verdict: rejected: 3.19x slower. Removing the L2 hit (forcing DRAM to supply 1x) is not worth it because (a) the 6x redundancy was already free via L2, and (b) the 1024-thread block collapses occupancy to 1 block/SM and adds per-tile __syncthreads. Confirms the attention kernels are at their practical ceiling and the 6x redundancy is not a real bandwidth cost.
